 Bam Adebayo recorded 35 points (14-of-20 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 This was a big night for Adebayo, who recorded his first double-double of the season with new highs in points and rebounds. Add in the assists, and it was a good night for those rostering the Heat captain. Even with there still being some bumps the Heat need to smooth over as they work Giannis Antetokounmpo into the fold, Adebayo has been close to a top-25 player in 12-team leagues. That’s encouraging, to say the least. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Bam Adebayo recorded 27 points (11-of-14 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists and three steals in Friday’s win over the Pacers. 
 After scoring 24 points in Wednesday’s win over the Hawks, Adebayo was even more productive against the Pacers. He shot 11-of-12 inside the arc, including 10-of-11 in the paint. Add in the rebounds and steals, and Bam had a good night. There’s still plenty of basketball to be played, but Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo appeared to have improved chemistry in Miami’s last two games.

 Bam Adebayo had 24 points (8-of-16 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists and three steals against the Hawks on Wednesday. 
 Adebayo bounced back nicely after scoring only eight points in Monday’s loss to the Mavericks. The 24 points Adebayo had are his season-high through five games. He’ll look to keep up his scoring against the Pacers on Friday. 
 Bam Adebayo 
 MIA 
 Center-Forward

 Bam Adebayo finished with 20 points (7-of-17 FGs), eight rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers on Saturday against the Hornets. 
 It has been a rough start to the year for Bam, but after totaling 19 points in Miami’s first two games, he was able to surpass that mark in this one. It wasn’t enough for them to get in the win column, but it was good to see him have a productive outing. He’ll try to build on this performance in their next game, which comes against the Mavericks on Monday.

 Bam Adebayo posted 15 points (6-of-12 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves. 
 After scoring six points on 3-of-9 shooting in the first half, Adebayo scored nine in the third quarter. Unfortunately for fantasy managers, the Heat center went scoreless in the fourth, attempting just one shot. The on-court chemistry between Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo needs work, which isn’t a surprise. But at times, Bam looked like little more than a bystander on offense, and that can’t happen.

 MIA

 Bam Adebayo (groin) and Pelle Larsson (illness) participated in Sunday’s practice. 
 Neither Adebayo nor Larsson played in the Heat’s final two preseason games, but both are on track to play in Wednesday’s regular-season opener against the Timberwolves. Adebayo’s status matters more to the Heat and fantasy managers because of his role in the rotation. As for Larsson, he’ll provide added perimeter depth off the bench. 
 Bam Adebayo 
 MIA 
 Center-Forward 
 #13 
 Bam Adebayo (groin), Pelle Larsson (illness) and Dru Smith (calf) are out for Wednesday’s exhibition against the Nets. 
 Adebayo is dealing with right groin tightness, and his absence frees up additional minutes for Nick Richards. With his contract for the upcoming season not being guaranteed unless he makes the Opening Night roster, this is a big opportunity for Richards. With Klay Thompson available, he’ll slide into the starting lineup spot Larsson occupied in Saturday’s loss to the Timberwolves. Smith’s absence won’t change anything regarding fantasy basketball, as starting point guard Davion Mitchell is available. 
 Bam Adebayo 
 MIA 
 Center-Forward 
 #13 
 Bam Adebayo logged 13 minutes in Saturday’s exhibition against the Raptors, tallying 10 points (2-of-7 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds and one three-pointer. 
 Because Saturday’s game was Miami’s first of the preseason, the team decided to shut down all five starters at halftime. Four of Adebayo’s seven shot attempts came from beyond the arc, including corner threes (both misses) on Miami’s first two possessions. With Giannis Antetokounmpo in the fold, Bam becoming a more consistent perimeter shooter is essential for the team’s offensive spacing. And that would also raise the center’s fantasy ceiling, so managers should watch this throughout the preseason. 
 Tyler Herro 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 According to multiple reports that have since been verified by their respective teams, Tyler Herro and Bam Adebayo got into a physical altercation on Friday morning in Las Vegas. 
 Once teammates, Herro was traded to Milwaukee as part of the deal that sent Giannis Antetokounmpo to Miami. According to reports, Adebayo took issue with some of the things Herro said on social media in the aftermath of the trade, and the situation came to a head on a practice court at the Resorts World Casino in Las Vegas. Adebayo reportedly struck Herro in the face, but it’s unclear whether the NBA or NBPA will open an investigation into the incident. 
 Bam Adebayo 
 MIA 
 Center-Forward 
 #13 
 Bam Adebayo (back) is out for the rest of Tuesday’s game against the Hornets. 
 Adebayo fell hard on his back during the second quarter of Tuesday’s Play-In Tournament game while trying to save a loose ball. He was subbed out at the ensuing deadball, taken to the locker room, and never returned. He was eventually ruled out for the remainder of the game during the third quarter, leaving Miami without one of its best players. Jaime Jaquez Jr. started in Adebayo’s place to begin the second half and could see more minutes if the team advances, depending on Adebayo’s status. 
 Bam Adebayo 
 MIA 
 Center-Forward 
 #13 
 Bam Adebayo posted a full line on Sunday with 25 points (11-of-18 FGs), 10 rebounds, three assists, three steals, two blocks and one three-pointer in a 143-117 win over the Hawks. 
 Adebayo wraps up the regular season with his third straight 20-point double-double while also contributing multiple defensive stats in each game. He typically isn’t quite as impactful in fantasy basketball as he is on the court for the Heat, but he has been a fantasy stud over the final couple months. Miami will be the 10th seed in the East, meaning they will travel to Charlotte for the play-in tournament next week. If Adebayo is playing this well, they will certainly have a chance to survive the tournament and make it to the playoffs.

 Devin Booker led the Suns with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), one rebound, eight assists, three steals and four three-pointers in a 117-104 win over the Magic on Thursday.
 Booker has had a few rough performances early on this season, but this has been an excellent two-game stretch for him. He has scored at least 30 points in back-to-back games, and he set a new season high for assists, steals and three-pointers in this one. Outside of a dud game against the Thunder, Booker has been excellent this season. He’ll continue to have the ball in his hands, and if he’s shooting the ball this well, the results will continue to be great for fantasy managers.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Miles Bridges stuffed the stat sheet on Thursday with 18 points (6-of-10 FGs), 13 rebounds, five assists, two steals and three three-pointers against the Magic.
 With both Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach in foul trouble, Bridges was able to step up on the glass. He ended up setting a new season high for rebounds in what has been an excellent start to the year for him, especially as of late. Over his last four games, Bridges has averaged 20.3 points, 9.0 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 2.3 steals, 1.0 block and 3.0 triples per game while shooting 51.8 percent from the free throw line. He has been fantastic in fantasy basketball and will look to stay hot against the Rockets on Saturday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Dillon Brooks posted a full line on Thursday with 24 points (9-of-16 FGs), one rebound, one assist, two steals, one block and four three-pointers against the Magic.
 Brooks’ scoring has dropped off this season, but he has made up for it with improved efficiency. However, he was able to do both in this game, which led to his best scoring performance of the season. Brooks has shot at least 55 percent from the floor in three of his last four games, which has helped his value in nine-category leagues. He likely won’t continue to shoot this well, but he certainly has the hot hand right now.

 Oso Ighodaro started on Thursday and finished with two points (1-of-2 FGs), five rebounds, one assist and one block against the Magic.
 Head coach Jordan Ott made the call to replace Khaman Maluach with Ighodaro in the starting unit. Unfortunately, Ighodaro found himself in foul trouble throughout the game, which prevented him from providing much value. Ighodaro is worth considering as a waiver wire pickup, even if this first game as a starter was rough. He won’t do much scoring, but he’s a strong passer for a big man and has five blocks over his last three games.

 Tristan da Silva provided a boost off the bench with 18 points (6-of-15 FGs), two rebounds, one assist and four three-pointers against the Suns on Thursday.
 All season long, da Silva has been a solid source of offense off the bench for Orlando, and he was able to provide that once again in this game. Unfortunately, he hasn’t been able to provide much outside of points and three-pointers, outside of a singular double-digit rebounding game last week. Aside from that night, da Silva hasn’t had more than four rebounds in a game. He’ll continue to score, but noting else will come consistently.

 Carter has had a few 20-point games this season and a few 10-rebound games, but he hadn’t done both at the same time until this game. He also set new season highs for both categories in what ended up being his best performance of the season. WCJ has been excellent to start the year, though he has had a four poor games mixed in. In all likelihood, WCJ will continue to provide inconsistent value, with a combination of big games and duds mixed in.

 Franz Wagner recorded a double-double on Thursday with 15 points (7-of-13 FGs, 1-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, 15 assists, four steals and six turnovers in a 117-104 loss to the Suns.
 With both Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) out, Wagner has stepped up as the team’s primary playmaker. That has led to some incredible assist numbers this season. He matched his previous career high for dimes last week before setting it last weekend. He set a new career high for assists once again in this game. Wagner has taken on a lot of responsibility on both ends of the floor, but he hasn’t excelled as a scorer. Still, he has been productive in other categories while trying to keep Orlando afloat until they get healthier.
 -  Noah Rubin
